content:
Dear Connections Today I am really excited to share this news with all of you that I recently had the opportunity to present my research paper titled "The Role Of Conflict-Induced Displacement In Expanding Cross-Border Trafficking Of Women And Children" at the 1st Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Seminar on Women's Rights Organised by the Lions Club of Kolkata City of Joy in collaboration with Jadavpur University alongside my Co-author Jiya Sarkar on 22nd July 2026.

About the Paper :- Our Paper basically examines the ways through which refugee and internally displaced people especially women and children are made even more vulnerable to human trafficking during and after a conflict. This research paper also concerns itself with examining the reasons why women and children are particularly vulnerable to human trafficking by looking into the social, economic, cultural, and political elements that put them at a greater risk.

Through this research paper an attempt had been made by us in understanding the true reasons behind this increasing heinous crime of trafficking and to analyse why despite of strong laws and international agencies like UHCR, IOM, UNICEF the issue of cross-border trafficking in South-Asian countries like India is still a highly neglected issue. 

While Working on this research paper it gave me the opportunity to explore various international laws and conventions such as the Palermo Protocol, CEDAW, CRC as well as Indian laws such as the Immoral Trafficking (Prevention Act), 1956, BNS Sections 143-144 and various other laws and treaties made for the safety and protection for women and children from exploitation and heinous crimes like trafficking and slavery. 

Lastly I would like to acknowledge my wonderful and brilliant Co-author Jiya Sarkar for her efforts and dedication, without her support and hardwork this couldn't be made possible for me.
comment: Beyond legal frameworks, a key challenge is ensuring protection systems reach displaced communities early, where lack of documentation, livelihood options, and safe reporting channels often enable traffickers.
